purpose: Auditable CUAI process, reliability, measurement and operating-improvement backlog. Entries record evidence, proposed change, expected benefit, risk, validation, status, result and rollback.

entries.evidence: Multiple recent published articles referenced /assets/site.js while the canonical article template references /assets/app.js; production /assets/site.js returned 404 and affected pages therefore lacked reliable CUAI custom editorial events.
entries.proposedChange: Restore /assets/site.js as a backward-compatible loader for /assets/app.js and make validation fail when a new article references a missing shared script.
entries.expectedBenefit: Restore custom editorial measurement on historical pages and prevent recurrence.
entries.result: PR #131 merged; historical custom-event history before repair remains quality-labeled incomplete where the script was missing.
entries.rollback: Revert PR #131 and the validator change.

entries.evidence: The optional Search Console query embedded in the GA4 endpoint was incompatible. Two speculative GA4-query repairs failed Production validation and were rolled back; an isolated direct Search Console read path was then validated using existing read-only credentials.
entries.proposedChange: Use the isolated direct Search Console API read path for aggregate search-performance reporting instead of retrying incompatible GA4 Core Reporting combinations.
entries.expectedBenefit: Restore search reporting without risking core GA4.
validation: Production endpoint HTTP 200 with siteFullUser aggregate data
entries.result: PR #136 merged; direct Search Console is the validated fallback while the optional embedded GA4 query remains isolated and non-blocking.
entries.rollback: Revert PR #136; core GA4 is independent.

entries.evidence: The source-health ledger became stale and a bounded refresh missed its internal deadline.
entries.proposedChange: Refresh the existing registry and recent primary sources; treat overdue queued improvements as handoff conditions.
entries.expectedBenefit: Reduce stale-source and broken-link risk without burdening the daily publisher.
entries.result: Recovered August 19; source-health state is current through 2026-08-19 with temporary-unavailable status preserved conservatively.
entries.rollback: Revert only inaccurate source-status or redirect changes.

entries.evidence: Buffer authoritatively showed tracked posts as sent while repository queue items repeatedly remained scheduled.
entries.proposedChange: Reconcile an exact Buffer-sent item to the existing queue item in place without creating a replacement or calling the scheduler.
entries.expectedBenefit: Keep delivery state authoritative and prevent duplicate recovery risk.
validation: exact queue-item/postId plus non-null sentAt required
multiple later sent-state recoveries used the rule successfully
entries.result: Exact-match reconciliation is established and has been applied repeatedly without duplicate posts or scheduler calls.
entries.rollback: Revert only incorrect sent-state fields if exact evidence is later disproved.

entries.evidence: Experiment cohort counts diverged between daily-cycle/coverage ledgers and management guidance.
entries.proposedChange: Reconcile experiment cohort status against current production ledgers during every CEO run before changing strategy state.
entries.expectedBenefit: Prevent conflicting agent instructions and accidental experiment overrun.
validation: daily-cycle and coverage ledgers independently agreed
entries.result: Cross-ledger synchronization is now a CEO reporting discipline.
entries.rollback: Revert only management-state wording if underlying production evidence is later shown wrong.

entries.evidence: A strong general credit-union governance story passed the prior relevance rule despite lacking a substantive AI/technology thesis.
entries.proposedChange: Require every future full article to have a substantive, source-supported AI or technology operating implication; never manufacture an AI angle.
entries.expectedBenefit: Reduce brand dilution while preserving broad functional coverage through technology/AI lenses.
validation: publishing rules and publisher policy aligned
hard stop added without weakening sourcing
entries.result: The publisher now requires substantive AI/technology mission fit prospectively.
entries.rollback: Revert the August 21 mission-fit policy edits; published content is unaffected.

entries.evidence: At experiment open, OSFI/RBFCU/Velera produced 5 rolling-seven-day Search Console clicks and Google organic was 6 sessions / 4 engaged / 66.7% engagement. The treatment added contextual links and allowed search evidence only as a tie-breaker between otherwise-equivalent editorial candidates.
entries.proposedChange: Run a bounded 14-day search-compounding treatment while preserving sourcing, mission fit, material-news priority and coverage diversity.
entries.expectedBenefit: Convert emerging organic visibility into qualified acquisition without turning CUAI into an SEO-led newsroom.
validation: feature branch and READY Preview validated at launch
September 1 review used exact Production GA4 and direct Search Console
entries.result: Stopped early on September 1 under the experiment's own quality trigger. Search Console for August 25-31 shows the treatment cluster at 1 click, entirely Velera, versus the 5-click baseline and >=8 target. GA4 Google organic reached 8 sessions but only 3 engaged, 37.5% versus the >=50% guardrail at a usable sample of 8. OSFI and Velera rankings remain strong at positions 2.7 and 7.28, so the result does not indicate ranking collapse. The search-supported editorial topic tie-breaker is removed. Existing contextual links remain only where independently editorially useful and will not be expanded as part of this stopped treatment.
entries.rollback: Search-supported editorial tie-breaker removed from growth guidance. Existing schedules, sourcing and factual content unchanged.

entries.evidence: Repeated recoveries were required because Alert quantity semantics were duplicated across multiple policy/runbook/state surfaces.
entries.proposedChange: Enforce max-one/no-quota semantics across authoritative policy while preserving compatibility-sensitive legacy state metadata until consumers can be ruled out.
entries.expectedBenefit: Prevent repeated policy drift without blind schema deletion.
entries.result: PR #151 closed the repeated Alert-quota drift class while preserving legacy non-authoritative metadata for compatibility.
entries.rollback: Revert PR #151 to remove the consistency validator.

entries.evidence: The August 25 publisher task ran but left no dated article, non-publication or blocker state, making a legitimate quality-gated no-publication indistinguishable from a failed/missing run.
entries.proposedChange: Require every scheduled article cycle to persist one dated machine-readable outcome: published, no-article-published with evidence, or blocked with exact blocker when GitHub is writable.
entries.expectedBenefit: Make publisher outcomes auditable and recoverable without increasing publication pressure.
validation: August 26 and subsequent cycles persisted complete dated outcomes
entries.result: Prospective observability contract is working; the historical August 25 outcome remains unknown rather than reconstructed.
entries.rollback: Revert PR #149; published content and schedules are unaffected.

entries.evidence: The August 31 Operating System recovery was verified on the agent bus, but a source-controlled usage-ledger append was left pending because the previous runtime only used truncated bounded file retrieval and correctly refused to reconstruct a large append-only ledger from partial history.
entries.proposedChange: Use the exact current Git blob SHA to retrieve the complete UTF-8 ledger before any whole-file mutation, preserve every historical entry byte-for-byte in logical content, then append the missing verified recovery entry and the current CEO entry.
entries.expectedBenefit: Restore safe append-only workload attribution without truncating audit history and provide a reusable write pattern for large JSON ledgers.
validation: current file blob SHA resolved from main
Git blob retrieval returned the complete ledger through the August 28 final entry
no historical entry was discarded in the prepared replacement
new entries use operational-proxy only and contain no invented token/cost data
entries.result: Safe full-ledger retrieval is available in this runtime and is used in the September 1 reporting branch to close the prior append-path degradation.
entries.rollback: If validation finds any historical mismatch, revert only the September 1 ledger commit and retain the agent-bus recovery evidence.

entries.evidence: The qualified September 1 AI-law Alert handoff hit the same safe-edit limitation twice. The first recovery branch changed only assets/app.js and was correctly left unmerged because the authoritative Alert contract requires an atomic package. The second branch attempted the atomic state write, but compare against September 2 main showed automation/daily-cycle-state.json at +488/-3276, which would discard most audit history even though its Preview was READY.
entries.proposedChange: Make complete-blob retrieval and explicit history-preservation validation mandatory for Alert/state whole-file writes. Add an executable daily-cycle preservation validator and require connector-only runs to perform the equivalent branch-vs-main history check before merge.
entries.expectedBenefit: Prevent a recovery workflow from corrupting append-style newsroom state, turn repeated connector limitations into a deterministic safe-stop rule, and make READY Preview insufficient evidence when state history is destructive.
validation: new validator passes Node syntax check
synthetic one-entry history shrink is rejected
current unsafe recovery branch remains unmerged after compare proved destructive state shrink
authoritative Operating System policy now requires full-blob retrieval and a pre-merge preservation invariant
entries.owner: CUAI CEO / Reliability Watch / CUAI Operating System
entries.result: The destructive recovery path is contained and a durable non-destructive state-write contract is prepared on the September 2 CEO branch. The qualified Alert remains unpublished until a workflow can produce the complete atomic package without dropping history; no partial or destructive production change is accepted.
entries.rollback: Revert the September 2 Operating System policy and validator additions. The blocked recovery branches and Production content remain otherwise unchanged.

entries.evidence: The sitewide sponsored CAI banner previously used nonstandard source/medium/campaign query parameters, so CUAI could not reliably join its own banner interaction to downstream CAI acquisition under the established UTM convention.
entries.proposedChange: Standardize the existing sponsored banner destination to utm_source=creditunionainews, utm_medium=site_banner, utm_campaign=cai_early_access, utm_content=sitewide_banner and add a privacy-safe cai_banner_click event without changing the destination, disclosure or external authority.
entries.expectedBenefit: Make G5 CUAI-to-CAI demand generation measurable from the CUAI side and enable downstream CAI reconciliation without treating missing attribution as zero demand.
validation: PR #175 limited the change to assets/app.js
standard UTM fields now match normal analytics semantics
dedicated cai_banner_click event contains no PII or free-form reader input
subsequent Production and analytics checks remain healthy
entries.result: CUAI banner-side attribution is now standardized and privacy-safe. Downstream CAI sessions/intent still require CAI-side evidence before G5 progress can be claimed; unavailable is not zero.
entries.rollback: Revert PR #175 to restore the prior banner query parameters and remove the dedicated banner event.

entries.evidence: PR #176 staged a SAR-confidentiality Alert during candidate evaluation, but the same Operating System cycle later recorded a definitive no-Alert outcome for that candidate. Leaving the mergeable PR open created a contradictory future publication path.
entries.proposedChange: Treat any open Alert PR that contradicts a later same-cycle completion event as a material conflicting handoff; close or supersede it before the operating cycle is considered clean.
entries.expectedBenefit: Prevent rejected Alert candidates from becoming live later through stale branches and preserve the final operating decision as authoritative.
validation: later same-cycle no-Alert completion explicitly rejected the candidate
current main and live Alerts remained unchanged
PR #177 recorded the reliability recovery and workload entry
post-recovery Production remained READY with no runtime errors
entries.result: The stale conflicting Alert PR was contained without publishing rejected content. Future same-cycle contradictions are now a reliability condition rather than routine branch clutter.
entries.rollback: No production rollback is required; reopen the stale PR only if newer verified evidence supersedes the final no-Alert decision.

entries.evidence: Direct Search Console shows /news.html at 176 impressions / 0 clicks / position 14.54 over the seven days ending September 3 and 496 impressions / 0 clicks / position 16.75 over 28 days. The current title is generic while the visible H1 already states the specific page intent: AI News for Credit Unions.
entries.proposedChange: Run a metadata-only title/description experiment on /news.html, preserving the canonical URL, route, body, article ordering, editorial selection and publication cadence.
entries.expectedBenefit: Convert existing Google visibility into qualified visits without steering editorial coverage toward search demand.
entries.risk: low if changed with a narrow patch; elevated if the only available mutation requires whole-file replacement of the large shared static page
validation: repeated page-specific Search Console evidence supports the hypothesis
current metadata and H1 were directly inspected
whole-file replacement is not accepted as a safe way to implement this metadata-only treatment in the current CEO connector runtime
entries.result: Not opened as an active experiment in this run. The second experiment slot remains free until the metadata can be changed through a narrow, reviewable patch or equivalent safe edit path; no risky rewrite was merged merely to create activity.
entries.rollback: Not applicable until treatment is implemented; if later opened, rollback is metadata-only restoration.
